title: Marriage Rates
description: In 2023, Singapore saw 28,310 marriages, slightly down from the record 29,389 the previous year. The crude marriage rate was 6.4 per 1,000 residents, with over 2,000 more marriages than a decade ago. Inter-ethnic marriages made up 16.6% of the total in 2022.

The median age for first marriages under different legal frameworks varies slightly, reflecting diverse cultural practices.

title: Fertility Decline
description: Marriage trends in Singapore show a shift towards later marriages and a decrease in fertility rates. The median age at first marriage for brides increased from 28.1 years in 2013 to 29.5 years in 2023, indicating a trend towards marrying later. Additionally, the proportion of ever-married females aged 40 to 49 who were childless rose from 6.4% to 9.3%, reflecting changing family planning choices. The marriage rate for single men aged 15-49 was 47.0 per thousand in 2022, slightly below the peak rate of 47.5 in 2002.

title: Educational Impact
description: Marriage trends in Singapore show a rise in the median age at first marriage for both grooms and brides over the years. The number of marriages registered annually has remained relatively stable, with slight fluctuations. Divorce rates have seen minor increases, and educational attainment appears to influence family size, with educated women having fewer children on average.

title: Divorce Trends

The average number of marital dissolutions per year from 2020 to 2024 was 7,291, slightly lower than the 2015-2019 average of 7,536.

title: Singlehood Rise

The marriage rate for single women aged 15-49 increased over the past decade, reaching 45.5 per thousand in 2022. Singlehood rates among females aged 30-34 rose significantly from 2000 to 2011, indicating changing social dynamics.

title: Marriage Peaks
description: Marriage rates in Singapore have shown notable trends, with an increase in the marriage rate for single men aged 15-49 from 2012 to 2022. The number of marriages in 2022 reached a record high since 1961, while the median age for first-time brides was 28.8 years in 2017. Additionally, there was a decrease in marital dissolutions from 2021 to 2022, with a significant drop in Muslim divorces.

title: Ethnic Variations
description: The data highlights trends in marriage and marital dissolutions among different ethnic and religious groups. Non-Muslim marital dissolutions decreased from 2021 to 2022. The percentage of first-time grooms and brides has increased over the past decade. Historical data shows significant variations in marriage numbers for Malays under the UMLA, with an all-time high in December 1988 and a record low in February 1963.

title: Charter Marriages
description: In May 2018, a total of 1,752 marriages were registered under the Women's Charter, with 1,256 involving Chinese couples. The same month saw 352 inter-ethnic marriages and 281 marriages under the Muslim Law Act. A notable decrease in Malay marriages under the UMLA was observed, dropping from 232 in April to 133 in May.
